item.title: Murmurly 2.1.0
item.description:
Choose your microphone

Settings → General now has a microphone picker. Murmurly followed whatever macOS was set to, which is usually right and occasionally a cliff: wearing a headset while the Mac keeps recording its own array is the largest drop in accuracy available to you, and nothing said which device was live. Pick one and it's remembered by the device itself, not its place in a list, so it comes back when you plug it in — and if it's away, Murmurly says so and uses the system default until it returns.

The capsule now names the microphone when it isn't hearing anything, instead of leaving you to notice that the meter never moved. Let go without having said anything and it stays up to tell you, rather than vanishing like a broken shortcut.

The first run checks it can hear you

Allowing the microphone and being able to hear you are different things, and every way the second one fails looks the same afterwards: you hold the key, you speak, nothing happens. So the setup guide ends by opening the microphone and showing you the level moving and your words coming back — on the same device and the same recognizer dictation itself uses. If nothing arrives it names the device and offers another; if sound arrives without words, it says so, which is usually the language.

About Murmurly

A real About window, in place of the system panel. It says which version you're running and, more usefully, what this install actually does with your words — cleanup on your Mac, or the name of the cloud model it's pointed at, stated plainly rather than left to a setting you'd have to go and read.
